title: Small colimits of ordinary presentable objects
statement: Fix a universe $\mathcal U$; sets and indexing categories called small belong to $\mathcal U$, and all Hom sets are small. An infinite cardinal $\eta$ is regular when a union of fewer than $\eta$ sets of cardinality less than $\eta$ has cardinality less than $\eta$. A category is $\eta$-filtered when every diagram with fewer than $\eta$ morphisms admits a cocone; for a poset this means that every subset of cardinality less than $\eta$, including the empty subset, has an upper bound. An object is $\eta$-presentable when its Hom functor preserves small $\eta$-filtered colimits. Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, $\eta$ an infinite regular cardinal, and $D:K\to\mathcal C$ a small diagram whose indexing category has fewer than $\eta$ morphisms. If every $D(k)$ is $\eta$-presentable and $D$ has a colimit $L$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], then $L$ is $\eta$-presentable.
